files_reviewed: health_monitor.py (lines 1-80, 195-225, 385-612, plus grep of the rest)
monitor/benchmark/particle_utils.py, physics_cupy.py, visualizer.py, gpu_setup.py, workloads.py (grep for random, fake and placeholder values)
note: No hosted model API. The only AI use is a local Aya model in a CI job that translates the README. The web dashboard has no login of any kind. Its admin check reads whether the server process is elevated, not who is calling. config.yaml binds it to 0.0.0.0. server.py also has unreachable code after a return (lines 698-715) and a second POST /api/processes/terminate handler (lines 968-995) that FastAPI never reaches. AlertEngine.check replaces active_alerts on every status poll, so auto-terminate notices vanish within seconds. No database rules labels apply because SQLite is local and server-side only.

labels.what: Shipped config binds the dashboard to 0.0.0.0, so every machine on the network reaches the unauthenticated API that kills processes, shuts down, updates and restarts the app
Web host is 0.0.0.0 in config.yaml but 127.0.0.1 in DEFAULT_CONFIG, so the same setting has two different values
Process terminate endpoint only checks app.state.is_admin, which says whether the server process is elevated. Any caller, local or on the network, can kill any PID once the app runs in admin mode
POST /api/shutdown has no auth or confirmation on the server. Any caller can stop the monitor
POST /api/update/install has no auth. Any caller can make the app download a release zip and overwrite its own files

POST /api/restart_elevated has no auth and takes a caller-supplied args list. With inplace true it execv-restarts the app with those args, for example --admin, which unlocks process killing. Windows only

Setting or clearing VRAM caps (POST and DELETE /api/vram_caps, lines 717-966) has no admin check on the server. Only the UI disables the slider and input for non-admins. A new cap immediately triggers auto-kill of watched PIDs when the server is elevated
The --admin command-line flag alone sets is_admin to true, even when the sudo or UAC relaunch fails or is declined. Admin is a launch flag, not a checked identity
Process list (with command lines and usernames), open ports, launch args and elevation status are served to any caller with no login
State-changing POSTs that take no JSON body (shutdown, update install, benchmark start and stop) have no origin or CSRF check. Any web page the user visits can fire them at localhost

Simulation WebSocket has no auth or origin check and takes particles, backend multiplier and spawn count from the client with no bounds. It runs a 3600 second GPU load, so any page can start a heavy GPU job
Benchmark start accepts any duration, matrix size and particle count with no server bounds. temp_limit=0 turns the thermal stop off. The 10-300 s and 0-100 C limits exist only as HTML slider limits
VRAM watcher also kills every other process on the GPU with the same name as a watched PID, even when that process is not in the watchlist

Committed watchlist of 13 PIDs from the author's machine loads at startup as if it were the user's choice. In admin mode any unrelated process that reuses one of these PIDs on a GPU over its cap gets killed
Committed runtime state sets a 16 percent VRAM cap on GPU 0. It loads at startup, so a fresh install alerts and can auto-kill once GPU 0 passes 16 percent
Updater downloads the release zip with no checksum or signature, runs zipfile extractall with no path check, then copies every file over the install
Update source is hardcoded to github.com/DataBoySu/MyGPU in two places, not the solusops/MyGPU repo this code ships from
Fallback CURRENT_VERSION is 1.2.0 while the package version is 2.1.0. If the import fails, every release looks newer

Process name and username go into innerHTML unescaped, and so do port process names at lines 369-384 and alert text in utils.js line 64. A local user can name a process with HTML to run script in the dashboard, which can then call the kill endpoints

UI says Quick runs 15 s, Standard 60 s, Extended 3 min, all at 4096x4096. The server ignores mode and runs 30 s at matrix 2048 unless Custom is chosen, because BenchmarkConfig.from_mode is never called
Default particle count is 30000 in the dataclass but 100000 in the router and in BenchmarkConfig.custom. Default matrix size is 2048 on the server and 4096 in the UI

CPU, memory and disk alert thresholds are hardcoded at 95, 95 and 90. The cpu_usage_warn, memory_usage_warn and disk_usage_warn values of 90 in config.yaml are never read, so CPU and memory differ from the config
cluster.name is set twice to two different strings, and cluster.nodes for multi-node monitoring is never used by any collector
History metric list is hardcoded to GPU 0, so other GPUs never appear in the history view
VRAM cap saved toast fires on any HTTP 200, but the server returns 200 with status error for bad input, so the UI reports success when nothing was saved
Watchlist checkbox stays ticked when the server answers Admin privileges required with HTTP 200, so the process looks watched but is not saved
Shutdown overlay turns green and says System Offline after a 3 second setTimeout, whatever the server did. Fetch errors are swallowed
Check for Updates only shows the latest GitHub tag as a success toast. It never compares with the installed version or uses /api/update/check, and an API error shows Latest version: undefined
Enforce option allocates a dummy GPU buffer the size of the cap. It does not limit any process to the cap, and on most cards it leaves less room than the cap implies
macOS notification builds an AppleScript string from title and message with no escaping. Inputs are numeric today, so it is a latent injection point
Dashboard loads chart.js unpinned (latest) plus other CDN scripts with no integrity hash, on a page that can kill processes
Installer pipes the uv install script from the internet into sh
Prompt says never modify HTML tags, href or src and keep Markdown links exactly. The code check after translation only tests length and a phrase list, so changed links pass through
Model-translated READMEs are committed and pushed straight to the branch on every README push, with no review step
workflow_dispatch input is interpolated straight into a shell run step in a job with contents write permission. Only users with write access can trigger it
